pages.text: After class, Julia gets out her paints. "Toby, I will paint you," she said. "Sit still."
pages.picture: Julia kneeling on the lawn with her paints and a big sheet of paper on a board; Toby posing proudly in front of the playhouse, sitting very straight

pages.text: Toby sits as still as a rock. Julia paints his white scales, his tail and his big feet.
pages.picture: Julia painting Toby; her painting of a white dragon is on the board; Toby sitting as still as a rock, chin up

pages.text: "It is the best painting!" said Julia. "Wait here. I will get a drink."
pages.picture: Julia running up the stone back step into the house; her painting left on the board on the grass by the paints; Toby sitting still in the middle of the lawn

pages.text: When she gets back, the paint pots are on the grass. There is paint on the play house, on Toby, and on her painting!
pages.picture: Julia on the back step with a glass of juice, shocked: the paint pots are tipped over on the grass, splashes of pink, blue and green paint on the playhouse walls, on Toby and all over her painting; Toby sitting in the mess, sad; nothing is floating
Julia holding up her ruined, paint-smeared painting, upset; Toby beside her still splashed with pink, blue and green paint; paint splashes on the playhouse

pages.text: Toby looks down. His tail droops. He is too sad to say a thing.
pages.picture: Toby splashed with pink, blue and green paint, head low, tail drooping flat on the grass, very sad; tipped paint pots around him

pages.text: Julia stamps her foot. Then she sits on the back step and sulks.
pages.picture: Julia sitting on the stone back step with her arms folded, sulking; Toby small in the distance by the paint-splashed playhouse

pages.text: But Toby looks so sad. And he has pink paint on his nose.
pages.picture: close-up of Toby, still splashed with paint, very sad, a blob of bright pink paint on the tip of his nose, looking hopefully toward Julia

pages.text: Julia grins. "Toby, you have a pink nose!" She wipes it off, and he grins back.
pages.picture: Julia kneeling, wiping the pink paint off Toby's nose with a cloth, laughing; Toby grinning back; paint still splashed on him and on the playhouse
